([[Antioch, Tennessee]]) | college = [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] (2022–2023) | highlights = * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2023 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2023]]) * [[Wayman Tisdale Award]] (2023) * [[NABC Freshman of the Year]] (2023) * [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] (2023) * [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Rookie of the Year]] (2023) * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2023) * [[SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] MVP ([[2023 SEC men's basketball tournament|2023]]) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2022]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2022) * [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] (2022) }} '''Brandon Jordan Miller''' (born November 22, 2002) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class. He is widely expected to be a top three pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]]. ==Early life and high school career== Miller grew up in [[Antioch, Tennessee]], and attended Cane Ridge High School.{{cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/03/09/brandon-miller-leads-cane-ridge-basketball-first-tssaa-state-tournament/4621166001/|title=Brandon Miller, Cane Ridge headed to first basketball state tournament|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=March 9, 2021|access-date=November 8, 2022}} He was named the Tennessee Gatorade Player of the Year after averaging 23.3 points, eight rebounds, 4.3 assists, 2.6 blocks, and 2.3 steals per game during his junior season.{{cite web|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article255317056.html|title=KU Jayhawks basketball recruit Brandon Miller will pick college or pros next week|work=[[The Kansas City Star]]|date=October 27, 2021|access-date=November 8, 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/06/04/brandon-miller-lashae-dwyer-named-gatorade-tennessee-basketball-players-year/7546904002/|title=Brandon Miller, Lashae Dwyer named Tennessee Gatorade basketball players of the year|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=June 4, 2021|access-date=November 8, 2022}} Miller repeated as the Gatorade Player of the Year and was named [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] as a senior after averaging 24.1 points, 8.5 rebounds, 4.3 assists, and 2.3 steals per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/alabama-signees-jaden-bradley-brandon-miller-named-mcdonalds-all-americans|title=Alabama Signees Jaden Bradley, Brandon Miller Named McDonald’s All-Americans|first=Kate|last=Windham|website=[[SI.com]]|date=January 25, 2022|access-date=November 8, 2022}} He also played in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and the [[McDonald's All-American Game]].{{cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2022/03/16/brandon-miller-tennessee-gatorade-boys-basketball-player-year-alabama-signee/7063849001/|title=Brandon Miller named Tennessee Gatorade boys basketball player of year|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=March 16, 2022|access-date=March 28, 2023}} ===Recruiting=== Miller was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services. His first scholarship offer was from [[Tennessee State Tigers basketball|Tennessee State]] who are coached by his cousin, [[Brian Collins (basketball)|Brian Collins]].{{cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/09/08/tennessee-high-school-basketball-cane-ridge-brandon-miller-explains-his-final-four/5738899001/|title=Brandon Miller on G-League, TSU, not picking Tennessee Vols basketball|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=September 8, 2021|access-date=March 28, 2023}} On November 1, 2021, Miller committed to playing college basketball for [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] after considering offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and Tennessee State.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32527284/top-15-forward-brandon-miller-gives-alabama-crimson-tide-second-five-star-commitment-2022|title=Top-15 forward Brandon Miller gives Alabama Crimson Tide second five-star commitment for 2022|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=November 1, 2021|access-date=November 8, 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/11/01/brandon-miller-five-star-forward-commits-alabama-basketball/6215359001/|title=Brandon Miller commits to Alabama basketball: 5-star from Cane Ridge|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=November 1, 2021|access-date=November 8, 2022}} He also considered playing professionally in [[National Basketball League (Australia)|Australia's NBL]] or the [[NBA G League Ignite|G League Ignite]].{{cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/09/03/cane-ridge-forward-brandon-miller-names-top-four/5712509001/|title=Cane Ridge's Brandon Miller narrows top-four|work=[[The November 14, 2022 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Miller was named to the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]] and [[Julius Erving Award]] watch lists entering his freshman season at Alabama.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Alabama-Basketball-Brandon-Miller-named-to-Naismith-Trophy-preseason-watch-list-197090157/|title=UA's Brandon Miller named to Naismith Trophy preseason watch list|first=Charlie|last=Potter|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=November 7, 2022|access-date=November 8, 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/alabama-guard-brandon-miller-named-julius-erving-award-watch-list|title=Alabama Guard Brandon Miller Named to Julius Erving Award Watch List|website=[[SI.com]]|date=October 26, 2022|access-date=November 8, 2022}} On November 21, 2022, Miller earned his first [[Southeastern Conference|Southeastern Conference (SEC)]] Freshman of the Week honor.{{cite news|last1=Smith|first1=Mason|title=Brandon Miller Named SEC Freshman of The Week|url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/brandon-miller-named-sec-freshman-of-the-week|access-date=January 2, 2023|agency=Bama Central|issue=November 21, 2022|date=November 21, 2022}} On December 17, 2022, Miller scored 36 points and six rebounds against [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]].{{cite web |title=Gonzaga vs. Alabama - Men's Basketball 2022 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/401488386 |website=ESPN |publisher=ESPN |access-date=January 2, 2023}} He posted an Alabama freshman-record 41 points on February 22, 2023, in a 78–76 overtime win against [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]].{{cite news |last1=Rothstein |first1=Michael |title=Nate Oats defends Alabama response: 'Taking it very seriously' |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35727687/nate-oats-defends-alabama-response-taking-very-seriously |access-date=February 24, 2023 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=February 24, 2023}} Miller was named the Most Valuable Player of the [[2023 SEC men's basketball tournament]] after averaging 20.3 points and 11 rebounds over three games.{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2023/03/alabama-star-brandon-miller-named-most-valuable-player-in-sec-tournament.html|title=Alabama star Brandon Miller named most valuable player in SEC tournament|first=Nick|last=Alvarez|website=[[AL.com]]|date=March 14, 2023|access-date=March 24, 2023}} He finished the season averaging an SEC-high 18.8 points per game and also averaged 8.2 rebounds and 2.1 assists. At the end of the regular season, Miller was named the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]], the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Rookie of the Year]], and first-team All-Conference.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35804505/alabama-brandon-miller-named-sec-top-player-coaches-ap|title=Alabama's Brandon Miller named top SEC player by coaches, AP|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=March 7, 2023|access-date=March 21, 2023}} He was a consensus second-team All-American selection after being selected to the first teams of the [[Associated Press]] and ''[[Sporting News]]'' and the second teams of [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] and [[USBWA]] selections.{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2023/03/brandon-miller-is-alabamas-second-ever-consensus-second-team-all-american.html|title=Brandon Miller is Alabama’s second-ever consensus second-team All-American|first=Mike|last=Rodak|website=[[AL.com]]|date=March 15, 2023|access-date=March 21, 2023}} Miller was also named the [[USBWA National Freshman of the Year]] and the [[NABC Freshman of the Year]].{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2023/03/alabamas-brandon-miller-named-national-freshman-of-the-year-by-usbwa.html|title=Alabama’s Brandon Miller named national freshman of the year by USBWA|first=Mike|last=Rodak|website=[[AL.com]]|date=March 21, 2023|access-date=March 21, 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rocketcitynow.com/article/sports/brandon-miller-named-nabc-freshman-of-the-year/525-174b142d-dd22-4545-a03b-0c85abe103ca|title=Brandon Miller named NABC Freshman of the Year|first=Mo|last=Carter|website=[[WZDX|RocketCityNow.com]]|date=March 28, 2023|access-date=March 28, 2023}} Miller would struggle in the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament]], shooting just 19% from the field in Alabama's three games, the worst percentage by any player with 35 shot attempts in the tournament since 1985.{{Cite web|last=Nasser|first=Reese|date=March 24, 2023|title=Alabama’s Brandon Miller hits rock bottom never seen in NCAA tournament history|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/ncaabk/alabamas-brandon-miller-hits-rock-bottom-never-seen-in-ncaa-tournament-history/ar-AA1935KU|access-date=March 25, 2023|website=MSN|language=en-US}} Alabama would fall in the third round of the tournament to [[2022–23 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]], with Miller going 3-of-19 from the floor. After the season Miller announced that he would forgo the remainder of his collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/36006157/alabama-freshman-brandon-miller-entering-2023-nba-draft|title=Alabama freshman Brandon Miller entering 2023 NBA draft|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=March 30, 2023|access-date=March 30, 2023}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]] || 37 || 37 || 32.6 || .430 || .384 || .859 || 8.2 || 2.1 || .9 || .9 || 18.8 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Miller's father, Darrell Miller, played [[college football]] at Alabama as the tight end position.{{cite web|url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2023/01/13/alabama-basketball-brandon-miller-stats-nick-saban-nate-oats/69786568007/|title=Brandon Miller: Alabama basketball star grew up Tide fan in Tennessee|work=[[Tuscaloosa News]]|date=January 13, 2023|access-date=March 28, 2023}} His older brother, Darrell Jr., played college basketball at [[Fisk University]] and professionally overseas. Miller's older sister plays at [[Cumberland University]].{{cite web|url=https://theathletic.com/4097532/2023/01/25/brandon-miller-alabama-nba-draft/|title=How Brandon Miller, Alabama basketball’s star freshman, is mixing promise, production|first=Dana|last=O'Neil|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=January 25, 2023|access-date=March 28, 2023}} ===Firearm incident=== On February 21, 2023, a Tuscaloosa police officer testified that Miller brought a firearm to teammate Darius Miles that was used in the fatal shooting of 23-year-old Jamea Jonae Harris in Tuscaloosa earlier that year.{{Cite web|date=February 21, 2023|title=Police: Tide's Miller delivered gun used in shooting|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35707831/police-alabama-star-brandon-miller-provided-gun-used-shooting|access-date=February 22, 2023|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}{{Cite web|date=February 21, 2023|title=Alabama hoops star delivered gun in shooting, police say |url=https://apnews.com/article/Nate-Oats-Brandon-Miller-Alabama-Basketball-4efc92362b106b01ab0d0a2ee9a4ea6c|access-date=February 22, 2023|website=AP NEWS|language=en}} According to Miller's attorney, Miles had left the gun in Miller's vehicle after Miller dropped Miles off at a club. As Miller was on his way back to pick up Miles, Miles texted Miller, requesting that Miller bring Miles's gun. When Miller arrived, Miles told his friend Michael Davis that the gun was in the vehicle. Davis retrieved the gun and shot into a vehicle in which Harris was a passenger, while Harris's boyfriend returned fire, resulting in two bullets striking Miller's car. Miller's attorney stated that Miller had no knowledge of any intent to use the weapon.{{cite web|title=Brandon Miller ‘never touched the gun’ used in Darius Miles capital murder case, attorney says|url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2023/02/attorney-says-brandon-miller-never-knew-illegal-activity-would-occur.html|website=al.com}} According to the Tuscaloosa police officer's testimony, while Miles and Davis initially lied to officers about the incident, Miller’s account of the shooting almost exactly matched what investigators gathered from video evidence and other witness testimony.{{cite web |title=Alabama Basketball Alabama AD: Nate Oats did not have complete information about Brandon Miller|url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2023/02/alabama-ad-nate-oats-did-not-have-complete-information-about-brandon-miller.html|website=al.com}} Tuscaloosa County chief deputy district attorney Paula Whitley stated Miller faces no charges as a result of the incident. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://rolltide.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/brandon--miller/8260 Alabama Crimson Tide bio] {{navboxes|list= {{2023 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{USBWA National Freshman of the Year}} {{NABC Freshman of the Year}} {{Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Miller, Brandon}} [[Category:2002 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball players]] [[Category:All-American college men's basketball players]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Tennessee]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:People from Antioch, Tennessee]] [[Category:Small forwards]]
